drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Counsel,

Attached are our initial comments to the Share Purchase Agreement. We have kept the changes focused on standard deal mechanics: clarification of the purchase price timing, ordinary closing conditions, materiality/knowledge qualifiers for the financial statement representation, and customary limitations on indemnity exposure. We think these changes should help move the document toward a balanced signing draft.

Please let us know if Bellweather has concerns with the proposed indemnity cap/basket or the thirty-day closing mechanics, and we can discuss promptly.

Best,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the Seller the Purchase Price for the Shares by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller. The Purchase Price shall be as set forth in the applicable purchase price schedule agreed by the Parties at signing, subject only to any adjustments expressly stated in this Agreement.
edits.name: Purchase Price mechanics

edits.text: 2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days of signing, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in this Agreement, including delivery of customary transfer documents, evidence of authority, and any required third-party consents. Each Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to consummate the Closing within such period.
edits.name: Closing mechanics

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. Except as set forth in the disclosure schedules delivered by the Seller, the Seller represents that, to the Seller’s knowledge, the financial statements delivered to the Buyer have been prepared in good faith and fairly present in all material respects the financial condition of the Company for the periods presented, subject to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of notes where applicable.
edits.name: Seller financial statements representation

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. Subject to the limitations in this Section, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer against Losses actually incurred by the Buyer arising out of any breach of the Seller’s representations, warranties, or covenants in this Agreement, including liabilities required to be disclosed but not disclosed in the disclosure schedules. The Seller shall have no indemnification obligation unless aggregate indemnifiable Losses exceed 1% of the Purchase Price, after which the Seller shall be liable only for amounts in excess of such threshold. The Seller’s aggregate liability under this Section shall not exceed 10% of the Purchase Price, except in the case of fraud or willful misconduct. Claims for indemnification must be made within twelve months after Closing, except for claims arising from fraud or willful misconduct.
edits.name: Indemnity limits

receiver.message_back: Counsel, Buyer cannot accept the proposed package as drafted: the financial statement rep should not be limited to Seller’s knowledge/good faith, the indemnity basket should be a true tipping basket no higher than 0.5% with a cap of at least 20–25% of Purchase Price, and the 12-month survival period should be extended to 18–24 months with fundamental reps, taxes, authority/title, fraud and willful misconduct uncapped or separately capped at the Purchase Price. We can accept a 30-day outside closing framework, provided it includes a firm long-stop date, clear deliverables/consents, and no limitation on Buyer’s remedies if Seller fails to deliver closing conditions within its control.

drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Counsel,

We have revised the draft to address Buyer’s principal concerns. Seller can agree to an objective financial statement representation, a 0.5% true tipping basket, a 20% general indemnity cap, 18-month survival, and separate treatment for fundamental reps, taxes, authority/title, fraud and willful misconduct. We have also tightened the 30-day closing framework with a firm long-stop date, specified deliverables/consents, and preserved Buyer’s remedies for Seller-controlled closing failures.

We believe this package should bridge the remaining issues and allow the parties to proceed to signing promptly.

edits.text: 2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur as promptly as practicable and in any event within thirty days after signing, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in this Agreement. The thirtieth day after signing shall be the outside date, unless extended by mutual written agreement of the Parties. At or prior to Closing, the Seller shall deliver customary share transfer instruments, evidence of authority and incumbency, applicable resignations and releases if required by the Buyer, updated disclosure schedules to the extent permitted by this Agreement, and all required third-party consents and approvals identified in the disclosure schedules or otherwise required for consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby. Each Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to consummate the Closing within such period; provided that nothing in this Section shall limit the Buyer’s rights or remedies if the Seller fails to deliver any closing condition, consent, certificate, instrument, or other item within the Seller’s control.
edits.name: Closing framework revised with long-stop date and remedies preserved

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. Except as set forth in the disclosure schedules delivered by the Seller, the Seller represents that the financial statements delivered to the Buyer have been prepared in accordance with the accounting principles historically applied by the Company, consistently applied, and fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Company for the periods presented, subject to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of notes where applicable. The Seller further represents that the disclosure schedules set forth all liabilities required to be disclosed under this Agreement.
edits.name: Financial statement representation made objective

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. Subject to the limitations in this Section, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer against Losses actually incurred by the Buyer arising out of any breach of the Seller’s representations, warranties, or covenants in this Agreement, including liabilities required to be disclosed but not disclosed in the disclosure schedules. The Seller shall have no indemnification obligation unless aggregate indemnifiable Losses exceed 0.5% of the Purchase Price, after which the Seller shall be liable for all indemnifiable Losses from the first dollar. The Seller’s aggregate liability under this Section for breaches of representations and warranties other than Fundamental Representations and Tax Matters shall not exceed 20% of the Purchase Price. For purposes of this Agreement, Fundamental Representations means representations relating to authority, due organization and existence, capitalization, title to the Shares, and enforceability. Claims arising from Fundamental Representations, Tax Matters, fraud, or willful misconduct shall not be subject to the basket or the 20% cap; provided that claims for Fundamental Representations and Tax Matters shall be capped at the Purchase Price, and claims for fraud or willful misconduct shall be uncapped to the extent permitted by applicable law. Claims for indemnification for breaches of representations and warranties must be made within eighteen months after Closing, except that claims arising from Fundamental Representations, Tax Matters, fraud, or willful misconduct may be made until the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. Covenants shall survive in accordance with their terms, or if no term is specified, until fully performed.
edits.name: Indemnity economics and survival revised
